questions.text: What is each stage's postcondition, and where is it checked? Can a stage report complete while part of its input failed?
What should never be ingested from each source (CI mail, lockfiles, binaries, spam)? Is there a fixture for each?
What happens to an input never seen before: unknown type, empty file, a 404, a binary, a huge file?
Where are the caps? What does the reader see when one is hit?
What is the expected yield of each automated job, and what alerts on zero?
What evidence does each automated decision-maker (judge, filter, threshold) see? Is it what a human would use?
Which golden set measures quality? What is the bar, the per-item minimum and the interval?
Which user tasks must survive this change? Is there a before/after script for each?
Which learned or derived data does this rely on? Where is its source, as-of date and invalidation trigger?
How many entry points reach this pipeline? Can they be one?

budgets.measure: reconciliation query: complete rows with fewer outputs than inputs
hand-labelled random sample of 50 admitted items, with a Wilson interval
age of the oldest in-progress job

rules.title: fetch() result used in a file that never checks res.ok or status
rules.why: A 404 page or an error body gets parsed, stored and indexed as content.
rules.confirm: failing-test: serve a 404 fixture; assert it is rejected before indexing
rules.fixHint: check res.ok and the content type; add a timeout

rules.title: Ingest path throws on an unknown type or kind
rules.why: One new type fails the whole ingest instead of degrading to a generic type with a flag.
rules.confirm: failing-test: property test with arbitrary type strings; ingest throws
rules.fixHint: store with a fallback type and a flag; report it

rules.title: extract()/embed()/model call before any content screen
rules.why: Junk is paid for, then stored.
rules.confirm: failing-test: junk fixture suite (lockfile, CI mail, minified bundle) reaches the paid call

rules.title: status = complete after a try that swallows errors, or with no count reconciliation
rules.why: Failed embeddings or chunks hide behind a complete status.
rules.confirm: failing-test: make the embedding call throw; document ends complete

rules.title: Job logs done with 0 changes as success
rules.why: A filter removing 100% of candidates looks like a quiet night.
rules.confirm: measurement: funnel counts per stage show the filter removing ~100%

rules.title: Confidence thresholds stacked with AND, no funnel counts logged
rules.why: Each threshold is reasonable; together they block everything.
rules.confirm: measurement: precision vs coverage sweep on labelled candidates

rules.title: Learned note or report injected into a prompt with no source or as-of date
rules.why: A stale lesson beats fresh evidence.
rules.confirm: failing-test: seed a lesson contradicting the source; the answer follows the lesson

rules.title: Stage output accepted with no sanity bound (one segment, one label for everything, empty, output/input ratio far off)
rules.why: A stalled or collapsed stage still reports success and its junk flows downstream.
rules.confirm: failing-test: feed a degenerate stage output fixture; the pipeline still marks the item complete

verify.text: golden set: precision and recall per item plus the minimum, with Wilson intervals, against the baseline
junk and look-alike fixture suite: reject vs admit with reason codes
fault injection on every external call (throw, timeout, 404, empty body)
funnel log per automated job in shadow mode, then apply mode
task scripts on the old build vs the new one, then an axe scan
